question: Ni aina gani ya tovuti inafaa kutumiwa kupata vifungu vya kusoma vya Grade 4?
A: Tovuti yoyote inayotoa michezo ya kasi na zawadi
B: Tovuti salama yenye matini yanayolingana na kiwango chako cha darasa
C: Tovuti yenye matangazo mengi ya bidhaa za biashara
D: Tovuti ya watu wasiojulikana wanaotuma ujumbe wa faragha
why_right: Tovuti salama yenye matini yanayolingana na kiwango cha darasa inamsaidia mwanafunzi kupata vifungu vyenye mada lengwa.
if_A: Anaamini kwamba tovuti yenye michezo na zawadi ni mahali pazuri pa kupata vifungu vya kusoma.
if_C: Anaamini kwamba tovuti inayouza bidhaa ina matini ya kielimu yanayofaa.
if_D: Anaamini kwamba tovuti inayotumwa na wageni inaweza kuaminika kwa vifungu vya kusoma.
curriculum_excerpt: kusakura matini kwenye tovuti salama ili kupata vifungu vya kusoma vyenye mada lengwa

question: Mwanafunzi anaelekezwa kuchagua makala atakayosoma wapi?
A: Katika maktaba ya shule
B: Sokoni mjini kwetu
C: Shambani kwa babu
D: Dukani mwa mzee
why_right: Mwanafunzi anaelekezwa kuchagua makala katika maktaba ili kupata makala bora za kusoma.
if_B: Mwanafunzi anadhani makala za kusoma hununuliwa tu sokoni na si kuchaguliwa katika maktaba.
if_C: Mwanafunzi anadhani kusoma kunaweza kufanyika tu mahali pa kazi za shambani bila mpangilio maalum.
if_D: Mwanafunzi anadhani makala zote za kusoma zinapatikana kwenye maduka ya kawaida.
curriculum_excerpt: kuchagua makala atakayosoma katika maktaba

question: Wanafunzi wanapojadiliana matini walizosoma, wanapaswa kuzingatia jambo gani?
A: Kukuza msamiati kwa kujadili maneno mapya yaliyomo kwenye matini
B: Kushindana ni nani aliyesoma vitabu vingi zaidi darasani
C: Kukubaliana kila mtu aseme jambo moja tu bila kusikiliza
D: Kueleza kwa nini hawapendi kitabu chochote kile
why_right: Kujadiliana matini walizosoma kwa kuzingatia ukuzaji wa msamiati huwasaidia wanafunzi kujifunza maneno mapya kutoka kwenye matini.
if_B: Mwanafunzi anadhani mjadala wa matini ni mashindano ya idadi ya vitabu.
if_C: Mwanafunzi anaamini kwamba mjadala hauhitaji kusikilizana na wenzake.
if_D: Mwanafunzi anadhani mjadala wa matini unapaswa kulenga kukosoa bila sababu za msingi.
curriculum_excerpt: kujadiliana na wenzake matini ambazo wamesoma kwa kuzingatia ukuzaji wa msamiati

question: Light passes through frosted glass, but you cannot see clear shapes behind it. What type of material is frosted glass?
A: Opaque
B: Transparent
C: Translucent
D: Reflective
why_right: Translucent materials let some light pass through but scatter it, so objects behind them cannot be seen clearly.
if_A: Believes that any material that blocks a clear view also blocks all light.
if_B: Believes that if light passes through a material, you can always see clearly through it.
if_D: Believes that shiny materials behave the same way as materials that light passes through.
curriculum_excerpt: movement on light through different materials (transparent, translucent and opaque)

question: Which tax is shown on a shop receipt as an extra charge added to the price of goods?
A: Income tax
B: Value Added Tax
C: Bank interest
D: Bus fare
why_right: Value Added Tax (VAT) is a tax added to the price of goods and is shown on receipts issued by shops and retailers.
if_A: Believes every tax on a shop receipt is income tax paid on earnings.
if_C: Believes banks are the ones who charge taxes on goods bought in shops.
if_D: Believes any amount paid when buying something is a tax.
curriculum_excerpt: discuss income and value added tax (VAT) from receipts issued by shops and retailers as a form of tax

question: Ni tovuti ipi ni bora zaidi kusakura ili kupata kifungu cha kusoma chenye mada unayotaka?
A: Tovuti yoyote inayotoa zawadi za bure kwa wanaosoma vifungu vyake.
B: Tovuti ya marafiki ambayo mtu yeyote anaweza kubadilisha maudhui yake.
C: Tovuti salama yenye matini yanayolingana na kiwango changu cha kusoma.
D: Tovuti inayokuomba jina lako kamili, anwani yako na picha yako.
why_right: Mwanafunzi anapaswa kusakura kwenye tovuti salama zenye matini ya kiwango na mada anayoihitaji.
if_A: Anadhani tovuti zinazoahidi zawadi ni salama na zinafaa kwa kusoma.
if_B: Anaamini kwamba tovuti ambayo kila mtu anaweza kuibadilisha ni ya kuaminika.
if_D: Anafikiri kutoa taarifa zako binafsi mtandaoni ni sehemu ya kawaida ya kusakura.
curriculum_excerpt: kusakura matini kwenye tovuti salama ili kupata vifungu vya kusoma vyenye mada lengwa

sub_strand: 5.2.1 Extensive Reading: Fiction and Non Fiction Materials
question: A Grade 5 learner finds a book has too many hard words and does not interest them. What should the learner decide?
A: The book is good for them because it is hard
B: The book is not right for them right now
C: They must finish it because all books are equal
D: They should read it aloud to the whole class
why_right: A text is judged appropriate based on its language and interest, so a book with hard language and no interest is not right for the learner now.
if_A: Believes a hard book is always the best choice for a learner.
if_C: Believes every book is equally suitable for every reader.
if_D: Believes a difficult book should be shared with others before judging it.
curriculum_excerpt: judge the appropriateness of a reading text on the basis of language and interest.

question: What does a translucent roof do in a house?
A: Blocks all light out
B: Makes its own light
C: Lets light pass through
D: Stores light at night
why_right: A translucent roof lets light pass through it so the inside of the house gets light.
if_A: Believes a roof must stop all light from getting into a house.
if_B: Believes a roof can give out light like a bulb.
if_D: Believes roofs can save light and release it later.
curriculum_excerpt: windows, translucent roofs, artificial lighting

question: Ni kitenzi kipi kinaonyesha watu wawili wakitendeana?
A: kupendwa
B: kupendeka
C: kupendana
D: kupendesha
why_right: Kitenzi 'kupendana' kinaonyesha kwamba watu wawili wanatendeana kitendo cha kupenda.
if_A: Mwanafunzi anadhani kitenzi chochote chenye -w- kinaonyesha watu wawili wanaotendeana.
if_B: Mwanafunzi anadhani kitenzi chochote kinachoishia kwa -eka kinaonyesha watu wawili wanaotendeana.
if_D: Mwanafunzi anadhani kiambishi -esh- kinaonyesha watu wawili wanaotendeana.
curriculum_excerpt: kutendewa, kutendeka na kutendana katika mawasiliano

question: Cooking oil in a pan catches fire in the kitchen. What is the safest first action?
A: Pour water quickly onto the burning oil.
B: Carry the burning pan outside and run away.
C: Cover the pan with a tight lid.
D: Fan the flames with a cloth to cool them.
why_right: A tight lid cuts off the air the fire needs, which is a safe way to respond to a kitchen fire.
if_A: The learner believes water puts out every type of fire, including burning oil.
if_B: The learner believes moving a fire away from the house always makes it safe.
if_D: The learner believes air moving over a fire will cool it down.
curriculum_excerpt: Safety precautions when handling heat

sub_strand: 2.2 Preserving Crop Products: Fruits and Vegetables
question: Why does preserving fruits and vegetables help a community have food all year?
A: It means farmers never need to plant any more crops.
B: It keeps a steady supply of food when fresh produce is out of season.
C: It lets families sell fresh produce without any market.
D: It makes fresh produce cheaper to buy during harvest only.
why_right: Preserved fruits and vegetables can be eaten after the harvest season ends, which supports food security.
if_A: The learner thinks preserved food removes the need for farming.
if_C: The learner believes that preservation is a way to sell food without buyers.
if_D: The learner thinks preservation only affects price at harvest time.
curriculum_excerpt: How does preservation of fruits and vegetables enhance food security?

question: Ama wants to record the shoe sizes of 30 learners neatly. What should she draw?
A: A picture of a shoe for each learner
B: A single number written at the top of the page
C: A table with rows and columns for the sizes
D: A long paragraph describing each learner's feet
why_right: A table with rows and columns lets Ama record each learner's shoe size in an organised way.
if_A: Believes that a drawing of each item is the best way to record many data items.
if_B: Thinks one number is enough to record data from many learners.
if_D: Believes that data should be recorded in written sentences rather than organised layouts.
curriculum_excerpt: draw a table to record data from real life

question: When a class prepares sunken seedbeds together, what is the fairest way to share the work?
A: Let the strongest pupils do all the digging
B: Let one pupil choose every job
C: Share tasks equally so everyone takes part
D: Let the teacher do the digging alone
why_right: Sharing tasks and responsibilities among all learners reflects social justice and fairness in seedbed preparation.
if_A: Believes fairness means getting the job done as fast as possible.
if_B: Thinks the group leader should decide everything alone.
if_D: Thinks learners need not share responsibility for school tasks.
curriculum_excerpt: share tasks and responsibilities in preparation of seedbeds

question: Why should we use clean water for drinking?
A: To make the water taste sweeter and nicer
B: To make the water look clearer and brighter
C: To make the water cooler on hot days
D: To kill germs that can cause diseases like cholera
why_right: Clean or treated water has no germs, so drinking it prevents illnesses such as cholera.
if_A: The learner believes good taste shows that water is safe to drink.
if_B: The learner thinks clear water is always safe, so germs cannot be present.
if_C: The learner believes water temperature is the main reason to choose one water over another.
curriculum_excerpt: use of clean water

question: Msomaji akikutana na neno gumu katika makala, afanye nini ili apate maana yake?
A: Atumie kamusi kupata maana ya neno
B: Aruke neno hilo na aendelee kusoma
C: Abuni maana kulingana na hisia zake
D: Asubiri mwalimu amwambie maana
why_right: Kamusi hutoa maana sahihi za msamiati uliotumika katika makala, hivyo kuitumia ni njia sahihi ya kupata maana.
if_B: Mwanafunzi anadhani kuruka maneno asiyoyajua hakuathiri kuelewa makala.
if_C: Mwanafunzi anadhani maana ya neno inaweza kubuniwa bila kuthibitishwa kwenye chanzo.
if_D: Mwanafunzi anadhani mwalimu peke yake ndiye anayeweza kutoa maana za maneno.
curriculum_excerpt: kutumia kamusi kupata maana za msamiati uliotumika katika makala

question: Ukipokea ujumbe kutoka kwa mtu usiyemjua mtandaoni, unapaswa kufanya nini?
A: Kumjibu ujumbe huo ili ujue anataka nini kutoka kwako
B: Kumwambia rafiki yako wa darasani tu bila mtu mzima kujua
C: Kufuta ujumbe huo kisha kusahau kabisa kuhusu tukio hilo
D: Kumjulisha mwalimu, mzazi au mlezi wako mara moja
why_right: Kutoa habari kwa mwalimu, mzazi au mlezi mara moja ni hatua muhimu ya kujilinda na kulinda wengine mtandaoni.
if_A: Anaamini kwamba kujibu mgeni kunaweza kumaliza hatari bila kumwambia mtu mzima.
if_B: Anaamini kwamba wenzake wa darasani wanaweza kushughulikia ujumbe wa mgeni badala ya watu wazima.
if_C: Anaamini kwamba kufuta ujumbe kunatosha bila kutoa habari kwa mtu mzima.
curriculum_excerpt: kutoa habari kwa mwalimu, mzazi au mlezi wake endapo atapata ujumbe kutoka kwa watu asiowajua mtandaoni

question: Why is it important to say sounds accurately when you speak?
A: So that your voice can be heard from far away
B: So that you never have to think about what to say
C: So that other people can understand what you mean
D: So that you can speak faster than your friends
why_right: Saying sounds accurately helps other people understand the message, which is effective communication.
if_A: Believes that accurate sounds are about how far the voice carries.
if_B: Believes that accurate speech removes the need to plan what to say.
if_D: Believes that accurate speaking is mainly about speed.
curriculum_excerpt: articulate sounds accurately for effective communication

question: Juma anataka kusoma matini ya kumfurahisha katika maktaba ya shule. Kitendo cha kwanza anachopaswa kufanya ni kipi?
A: Kutambua aina mbalimbali za matini zilizopo maktabani
B: Kusoma kitabu cha kwanza anachokiona bila kukiangalia
C: Kumwomba mwalimu amchagulie kitabu cha kusoma
D: Kumaliza kusoma vitabu vyote vilivyopo maktabani
why_right: Kabla ya kusoma, msomaji anapaswa kwanza kutambua aina za matini zilizopo ili kuchagua inayomvutia.
if_B: Mwanafunzi anadhani matini yoyote inafaa bila kuzingatia kama inamvutia.
if_C: Mwanafunzi anaamini kwamba mwalimu pekee ndiye anayeweza kuchagua matini za kusoma.
if_D: Mwanafunzi anadhani ni lazima asome kila kitabu kabla ya kuchagua kimoja.
curriculum_excerpt: kutambua aina mbalimbali za matini ili kuchagua inayomvutia

question: Neno 'mashariki' linamaanisha nini?
A: Upande wa jua linapozama
B: Upande wa jua linapochomoza
C: Upande wa kaskazini wa ramani
D: Upande wa kusini wa nchi yetu
why_right: Mashariki ni upande ambao jua huchomoza, na kutafuta maana za maneno kama haya ni sehemu ya kujifunza.
if_A: Anachanganya mashariki na magharibi, ambapo jua hutua.
if_C: Anafikiri mashariki ni sawa na kaskazini kwenye ramani.
if_D: Anachanganya mwelekeo wa mashariki na kusini.
curriculum_excerpt: kutafuta maana za maneno kuhusu mada lengwa

question: Which of these materials is a good conductor of heat?
A: A wooden spoon
B: A plastic cup
C: An iron cooking pan
D: A woollen sweater
why_right: Iron is a metal that allows heat to pass through it quickly, so it is a good conductor.
if_A: The learner believes hard, solid materials that are not metal always carry heat well.
if_B: The learner believes stiff objects that feel firm must conduct heat easily.
if_D: The learner believes soft, warm-feeling materials are good conductors of heat.
curriculum_excerpt: Classification of conductors of heat into good or poor conductors

question: Why should a learner keep a record of the materials read?
A: To show the teacher how many pages were read in total.
B: To keep track of the books read and what was learned from them.
C: To prove that the learner owns every book in the school library.
D: To count how many books the school library bought this year.
why_right: A record of materials read helps a learner remember and track the books they have read and what they learned.
if_A: Believes that a reading record is only a way to show the teacher quantities for marks.
if_C: Believes that a reading record is proof of owning books.
if_D: Believes that a learner's reading record is used to count school library purchases.
curriculum_excerpt: keep a record of materials read

question: Which tongue twister practises the /s/ sound most?
A: Benny bakes big brown buns.
B: Sammy sells six sweet samosas.
C: Mama makes many mandazi.
D: Fred fries fish and fruit.
why_right: Sammy sells six sweet samosas repeats the /s/ sound in many of its words.
if_A: The learner thinks the /b/ sound is the main focus of any tongue twister with many words.
if_C: The learner believes that repeated vowel sounds matter more than consonant sounds in a tongue twister.
if_D: The learner confuses the /f/ sound with the /s/ sound because both are whispered sounds.
curriculum_excerpt: recognise the vowels sounds and diphthongs

question: A kiosk owner buys a loaf of bread for Ksh 60. She sells it for Ksh 45. How much loss does she make?
A: Ksh 105
B: Ksh 45
C: Ksh 15
D: Ksh 60
why_right: Loss happens when the selling price is less than the buying price, so Ksh 60 minus Ksh 45 gives a loss of Ksh 15.
if_A: Believes loss is found by adding the buying price and the selling price.
if_B: Believes loss is the same as the selling price.
if_D: Believes loss is the same as the amount paid to buy the bread.
curriculum_excerpt: calculate loss realized from sales of different items in the community

question: Which material lets light pass through so you can see clearly through it?
A: A thick wooden door
B: A sheet of brown cardboard
C: A clear glass window
D: A metal cooking pot
why_right: Glass is transparent, so light passes through it and we can see clearly through it.
if_A: Believes that solid materials like wood always let some light pass through clearly.
if_B: Thinks that any thin material lets light pass through it clearly.
if_D: Thinks that shiny objects are the ones that let light pass through them.
curriculum_excerpt: carry out activities to show the movement on light through different materials (transparent, translucent and opaque)

question: When light hits a plane mirror, how does the angle of reflection compare with the angle of incidence?
A: The angle of reflection is always zero
B: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection
C: The angle of reflection is twice the angle of incidence
D: Light bends when it hits the mirror
why_right: The laws of reflection state that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
if_A: Thinks that light does not reflect at an angle when it hits a mirror.
if_C: Believes the reflected angle grows larger than the incoming angle.
if_D: Thinks that light bends like it does when entering water instead of reflecting.
curriculum_excerpt: perform an experiment to show reflection of light on plane mirrors (laws of reflection)

question: Which of these is a homogeneous mixture?
A: Sand and water
B: Salt dissolved in water
C: Maize grains mixed with stones
D: Beans mixed with cooking oil
why_right: Salt dissolved in water forms one uniform mixture where the salt cannot be seen separately.
if_A: Learner thinks any mixture of a solid and a liquid is uniform because the parts can be seen mixing.
if_C: Learner thinks mixtures are uniform whenever the parts are of similar size and colour.
if_D: Learner believes that a mixture of two liquids that do not dissolve is uniform since both are runny.
curriculum_excerpt: categorise mixtures as homogeneous (uniform) and heterogeneous (non- uniform)

question: A cook needs to lift a very hot cooking pot from the fire. Which action is the safest?
A: Touch the pot briefly to test its heat
B: Pour cold water over the hot pot
C: Hold the hot pot with a dry oven glove
D: Hold the hot pot with a wet cloth
why_right: A dry oven glove protects the hand from heat, which is a safety precaution when handling heat.
if_A: Thinks a quick touch is harmless, so testing heat by touch is safe.
if_B: Thinks cooling a hot object suddenly makes it safe to handle.
if_D: Thinks any cloth protects the hand from heat, even when it is wet.
curriculum_excerpt: acknowledge safety precautions when handling heat

question: What is value added tax (VAT)?
A: A fee paid to rent a shop
B: A tax added to the price of goods
C: The profit a shop keeps
D: A discount given to customers
why_right: VAT is a form of tax that is added to the price of goods and is shown on shop receipts.
if_A: Confuses VAT with a fee charged for renting a shop or other premises.
if_C: Confuses VAT with the profit a shop makes on its sales.
if_D: Thinks VAT is an amount taken off the price to help customers.
curriculum_excerpt: discuss income and value added tax (VAT) from receipts issued by shops and retailers as a form of tax

question: Juma has a mixture of cooking oil and water in a bottle. Which method should he use to separate them?
A: Filtering through a cloth
B: Using a magnet
C: Using a separating funnel
D: Sieving through a fine mesh
why_right: A separating funnel lets the denser water drain out first, separating it from the oil that floats above.
if_A: Learner believes filtering works on liquids that do not mix, not only solids in liquids.
if_B: Learner thinks a magnet can pull liquids apart if they are different.
if_D: Learner thinks sieving can separate liquids that are mixed together.
curriculum_excerpt: Separating heterogeneous mixtures (Winnowing, picking, sieving, using magnet, Filtering, decanting, separating funnel)

question: Wanjiru counted 8 mangoes at the market. Which tally marks show the number 8?
why_right: A bundle of five strokes plus three single strokes makes 8 tally marks.
if_A: Learner forgets to count one stroke when reading the bundle of five and gets 6.
if_B: Learner thinks a bundle of five plus four strokes makes 9, so miscounts the total.
if_D: Learner thinks a group of four strokes is a complete tally group and miscounts the total as 7.
curriculum_excerpt: draw tally marks of the collected and any data

question: Kabla ya kufungua faili ya kifungu cha kusoma kwenye tarakilishi, unapaswa kufanya nini kwanza?
A: Kubofya vitufe vyote bila kuangalia jina la faili
B: Kuzima tarakilishi kabla ya kusoma chochote
C: Kutambua jina la faili lengwa kwenye tarakilishi
D: Kufuta faili zote zilizo kwenye tarakilishi
why_right: Mwanafunzi lazima kwanza atambue jina la faili lengwa kabla ya kulifungua na kulifunga.
if_A: Anafikiri faili inaweza kufunguka kwa kubofya ovyo ovyo bila kujua inaitwaje.
if_B: Anadhani tarakilishi lazima izimwe kabla ya kusoma faili yoyote.
if_D: Anaamini kufuta faili nyingi ni hatua ya kwanza ya kupata kifungu cha kusoma.
curriculum_excerpt: kutambua jina la faili lengwa kwenye tarakilishi

question: How does practising personal hygiene help us stay healthy?
A: It makes the hands smell nice so others like us
B: It removes germs that cause sickness from our bodies
C: It makes our skin lighter so we look healthier
D: It stops us feeling hungry until lunch time
why_right: Personal hygiene prevents communicable diseases by removing the germs that spread them.
if_A: Believes hand washing is mainly about making the body smell good.
if_C: Believes hygiene changes the natural colour of the skin.
if_D: Believes hygiene practices control how hungry a person feels.
curriculum_excerpt: Prevention of communicable diseases as learners practice personal hygiene.

question: How does a balanced diet affect our health?
A: The body gets heavier but not stronger
B: The body grows strong and fights sickness well
C: The body needs less water to stay well
D: The body stops needing sleep at night
why_right: A balanced diet gives the body the nutrients it needs to grow, stay strong and resist illness.
if_A: The learner believes that body weight alone shows how healthy a person is.
if_C: The learner believes that diet changes the body's need for water in a way that removes the need to drink.
if_D: The learner believes that eating well can replace the body's need for rest.
curriculum_excerpt: How does a balanced diet impact on health?

question: A triangle has a base of 8 cm and a height of 5 cm. What is its area in cm²?
A: 40 cm²
B: 13 cm²
C: 10 cm²
D: 20 cm²
why_right: The area of a triangle is half of base × height, which is ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 cm².
if_A: Forgets to take half of the base times the height, so finds the area of a rectangle instead.
if_B: Adds the base and the height instead of multiplying them.
if_C: Halves only one measurement instead of halving the whole product of base and height.
curriculum_excerpt: work out the area of triangles in cm2 using the relationship between a rectangle and a triangle

question: Chagua sentensi inayotumia kitenzi katika hali ya kutendeka kwa usahihi.
A: Mlango ulifungiwa upepo ulipovuma.
B: Mlango ulifungwa upepo ulipovuma.
C: Mlango ulifungika upepo ulipovuma.
D: Mlango ulifungana upepo ulipovuma.
why_right: Kitenzi 'fungika' kinaonyesha kwamba mlango umefungwa wenyewe bila mtu kuufunga, jambo linalolingana na hali ya kutendeka.
if_A: Mwanafunzi anadhani kiambishi -iwa kinaonyesha kitu kinachojifunga chenyewe.
if_B: Mwanafunzi anadhani kila umbo la kitenzi kinachoishia -wa linaonyesha kwamba mtu ameufunga mlango.
if_D: Mwanafunzi anadhani upepo ukisababisha kitendo, kitenzi lazima kionyeshe kutendana kati ya vitu.
curriculum_excerpt: kunyambua vitenzi katika hali lengwa akiwa peke yake, wakiwa wawiliwawili au katika vikundi

question: A class is making a presentation about a balanced meal. Why should every learner contribute ideas and work together?
A: So the team can share ideas and make a better presentation together.
B: So that one learner can finish the work quickly and alone.
C: So that the teacher does not need to check the work.
D: So that each learner can show only his or her own favourite food.
why_right: Working together and contributing ideas builds teamwork and unity, and results in a better presentation on healthy eating.
if_B: The learner believes that group work is best when one person does everything.
if_C: The learner thinks that group presentations are a way to avoid teacher checking.
if_D: The learner believes that a group presentation should show only one person's preferences.
curriculum_excerpt: Exhibit unity in making collaborative presentations of a balanced meal

question: Estimate 21 x 58 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. What is your estimate?
why_right: Rounding 21 to 20 and 58 to 60 gives 20 x 60, which is 1200.
if_A: Rounds 58 down to 50 and 21 down to 20.
if_C: Rounds only 58 to 60 and leaves 21 unchanged.
if_D: Rounds 21 up to 30 instead of down to 20.
curriculum_excerpt: estimate product by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten in different situations

question: Juma buys 3 kilograms of rice every week. Which expression shows the kilograms he buys in n weeks?
B: 3n
why_right: Buying 3 kilograms in each of n weeks gives 3 times n, which is written as 3n.
if_A: Believes that the weeks and the kilograms are added instead of multiplied.
if_C: Believes the number of weeks should be divided by the kilograms each week.
